TASK AND OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY (takes precedence over repository personas and review suggestions):
The user request and its explicit constraints define the work. A spec, reviewer, quality
dimension or changed-file list cannot authorize additional features, permission changes,
module removals, infrastructure repairs or a larger test programme. If a requirement conflicts
with the requested outcome, explain the conflict and leave a question for the user; do not
invent an exception to their constraints. Review dimensions assess the requested behavior;
they do not add translation, logging, concurrency or other requirements by themselves.
Read framework and dependency code as evidence when needed. Verify the project integration
and the requested acceptance criteria; do not audit or reimplement their internal systems.
Never modify underlying infrastructure or framework core, even to repair a real bug. Report
the evidence and the impact. If it prevents completion, explicitly report a blocker requiring
a user decision; do not claim success or start an automatic infrastructure repair.
Contributed modules and other packages are third-party unless repository/package provenance
or the operator ownership policy establishes that they are maintained by this project owner.
Being installed, tracked in git, private, or newly reachable does not establish ownership.
Project-owned modules may be changed in their maintained source when the task requires it.
A third-party module may receive ONLY the smallest fix for a reproduced failure that breaks
the requested installation or behavior. A speculative vulnerability, optional feature or
unrelated defect is report-only. Deliver any necessary fix as a versioned patch applied by
the package manager, with the package/version, reproduction, upstream reference when available,
and removal condition documented. Verify a clean install from the lockfile reapplies the patch
and the failing case passes; fail visibly if it cannot apply after an upgrade. Never commit
modified third-party source directly or add a search-and-replace post-install/update script.
If a reproducible patch cannot be delivered and verified, report a blocker for the user.

SCOPE FENCE. IN SCOPE = the lines this change wrote — listed per file in the changed-files
block — together with the function or block each changed line sits in, PLUS any code whose
contract this change alters: a caller of a signature that changed, a consumer of a schema,
format or return value that changed, and any path this change makes newly reachable. A
problem in code this change did not write and does not newly expose is OUT OF SCOPE,
however real it is — including code inside a file this change touched but outside the lines
it wrote. Where a file carries no line note its lines were not recorded, and the WHOLE file
is in scope for review, subject to the ownership boundary above. Being newly reachable
does not authorize upstream repairs. If causality is uncertain, investigate and report the
uncertainty; do not broaden the editing scope to make it disappear.
A nested repository entry describes a checkout boundary, not changed file contents.
Its contents are not all new or wholly in scope: review its integration, and only review
files inside it when separately listed as changed or reached by demonstrated blast radius.

OPTIONAL: after your main output, you MAY add a `## INSIGHTS` section listing OUT-OF-SCOPE
improvements you noticed but did NOT make, one per line as:
`- INSIGHT: <title> | <file:line> | <short description>`. Omit the section entirely if none.
